title: DataSpec
description: Structural specification of all entities, types, and relationships in a system. Source of truth for UML generation and cross-spec linting.

version.description: Semver string, e.g. '1.0.0'. Increment when any entity, field, or relationship changes.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the DataSpec schema this document conforms to. Must be '1.0.0'.

module.description: Human-readable name of the system or module this spec describes.

description.description: Optional high-level description of what this system does.

primitives.description: Allowed primitive type names. Every field type must resolve to one of these or to an entity/enum name.

id.description: Unique identifier for this primitive type

name.description: Name of the primitive type (e.g., string, number, boolean, array, object)

enums.description:
Enumerated types used across entities and API contracts.
Enum names must be unique and follow PascalCase.
Each enum must have at least one value following SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

values.description: All valid values for this enum.

entities.description:
All domain entities (classes) in the system.
Entity names must be unique and follow PascalCase.
Each entity must have at least one field marked as primaryKey (or the first field is assumed).
Abstract entities cannot be the target of composition/aggregation relationships.

description.description: What this entity represents in the domain.

abstract.description: If true, this entity cannot be instantiated directly. Used for base classes.

extends.description: Name of the parent entity this one inherits from. Must match an entity name in this spec.

fields.description:
Data fields on this entity.
Field names must be unique and follow camelCase.
Field types must resolve to a primitive, entity name, or enum name defined in this spec.
At least one field should be marked as primaryKey.

type.description: Primitive name, entity name, enum name, or array thereof (e.g. 'string', 'User', 'OrderStatus', 'string[]', 'OrderItem[]').

required.description: Whether this field must always be present.

example.description: A concrete example value. Used in test spec and documentation.

primaryKey.description: True if this field is the primary key for the entity. Only one field per entity should be marked as primaryKey. If not set, the first field or a field ending with 'Id'/'id' is assumed to be the primary key.

glossaryRefs.description: Glossary term IDs (GL-NNN) referenced in this field's description.

methods.description:
Methods exposed by this entity. Each must reference a function defined in the API spec.
Method names must follow camelCase.
apiRef must reference a function ID in the API spec (e.g. 'FN-createUser').

name.description: camelCase method name as it appears on the entity.

apiRef.description: The function ID in the API spec this method corresponds to.

visibility.description: Whether this entity is part of the public API surface or internal only.

glossaryRefs.description: Glossary term IDs (GL-NNN) that this entity maps to. The entity name itself should have a corresponding glossary entry.

relationships.description:
All directional relationships between entities.
Relationship types must be one of: association, composition, aggregation, dependency, realization.
Cardinality labels must be one of: 1, 0..1, 1..*, *, 0..*
No duplicate relationships of the same type between the same entity pair.
Abstract entities cannot be the target of composition/aggregation relationships.

type.description: Relationship type. 'association': general link. 'composition': target cannot exist without source. 'aggregation': target can exist independently. 'dependency': source uses target but does not own it. 'realization': source implements target interface.

cardinality.description: Multiplicity on each end of the relationship.

fromLabel.description: Multiplicity label on the source side, e.g. '1', '0..1', '1..*', '*'.

toLabel.description: Multiplicity label on the target side, e.g. '1', '0..1', '1..*', '*'.

label.description: Optional verb or role label on the relationship arrow, e.g. 'places', 'contains'.
